# Results — Study 334 (ARK-Innovation) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). ARKK (Cathie Wood's flagship
innovation ETF) tested three ways against the retail-hype story: a **trend / momentum /
mean-reversion** overlay race on the real daily tape, and the **dollar-weighted vs
time-weighted return gap** — the difference between what a buy-and-hold investor earned and
what the average dollar that walked in the door actually earned. Benchmarks: QQQ and XLK
(innovation-beta). Auto-adjusted (total-return-proxy) closes from `yfinance`. As-of
**2026-06-18**; the headline stats drop the partial month and run through the last complete
month, **2026-05-29**. Match the per-tape fingerprint to confirm you hold the same tape.*

## The arc — boom, bust, partial recovery (ARKK buy-and-hold, total-return proxy)

| Segment | Window | CAGR | Total return |
|---|---|--:|--:|
| Inception → peak | 2014-10-31 → 2021-02-12 | **+40.3%/yr** | **+737%** |
| Peak → as-of | 2021-02-12 → 2026-05-29 | **−11.3%/yr** | **−47%** |
| Full sample | 2014-10-31 → 2026-05-29 | **+13.8%/yr** | **+346%** |

ARKK peaked **2021-02-12** at ~$154 (from a $18.4 inception NAV), then fell **−81%** to a
2022-12-28 trough of ~$29, and sat at ~$82 as-of. The *price* did fine over the full
sample (+13.8%/yr) — but as the dollar-weighted section shows, almost nobody held it from
inception; the money arrived near the top.

## Was it a momentum win? — overlay race (real ARKK, gross, one-day execution lag)

| Overlay | mean (bps/day) | ann. Sharpe | HAC *t* | % days invested |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Trend — 50/200 SMA crossover** | **+6.45** | **0.60** | **+2.09** | 58% |
| Time-series momentum (1-day) | +4.16 | 0.39 | +1.36 | 53% |
| Mean-reversion (5-day, z<−1) | +0.74 | 0.09 | +0.33 | 24% |
| ARKK buy-and-hold (reference) | — | 0.53 | +1.88 | 100% |

- The **slow-trend (50/200) overlay** is the only one to clear the inference bar
  (HAC *t* = **+2.09**) — but barely: the circular block-bootstrap 95% CI on its daily mean
  is **[+0.22, +12.3] bps**, a lower bound a hair above zero. The edge is *real but thin*.
- It is almost entirely a **crash-avoidance** trick: it sits in cash for ~42% of days,
  largely 2021-22, sidestepping the −81% drawdown. Its **excess Sharpe over ARKK
  buy-and-hold is only +0.07** (0.60 vs 0.53) — and *far below QQQ buy-and-hold* (0.93).
- **Time-series momentum (*t* = +1.36) and mean-reversion (*t* = +0.33) are NONE.** ARKK's
  daily returns carry neither tradable persistence nor tradable reversal beyond noise.

## Could you trade it? — cost sweep (trend overlay, net)

| round-trip cost | net mean (bps/day) | Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 bps (gross) | +6.45 | 0.60 | +2.09 |
| 5 bps | +6.42 | 0.60 | +2.08 |
| 10 bps | +6.39 | 0.60 | +2.07 |
| 20 bps | +6.33 | 0.59 | +2.05 |

The 50/200 crossover trades rarely, so costs are *not* where it dies — but it never earns
more than holding QQQ would have, while running single-stock-of-a-fad concentration risk.
**Tradability — MIRAGE**: the only "edge" is dodging a crash, and a plain QQQ holder both
avoided ARKK's drawdown *and* compounded faster.

## The headline — the behaviour gap (dollar-weighted vs time-weighted)

ARKK is the textbook case of the **investor-return gap**. Morningstar's *Mind the Gap*
research and widely-reported flow analyses (Arnott / Morningstar 2023; Leverage Shares and
FT reporting 2023) found that although ARKK's *time-weighted* return over its big years was
positive, the **dollar-weighted (money-weighted) return the average investor earned was
deeply negative** — because the bulk of ARKK's assets arrived in 2020-early-2021, right
before the −81% fall. Morningstar estimated ARKK destroyed on the order of **$7–10 billion**
of investor wealth on a dollar-weighted basis over 2014-2023 even as the fund's posted
return looked respectable. We *cannot* reconstruct the exact real gap here (ARKK's
shares-outstanding history is not on the public daily feed; `data.fetch_flows` returns
`None`), so the real figure is quoted from that literature, and the **mechanism is
demonstrated on the deterministic synthetic control** below. The real-tape numbers above
that we *can* compute (a +737% boom to 2021-02 followed by a −81% drawdown) are exactly the
price arc that turns a positive headline return into a negative investor experience.

## Synthetic control — the behaviour gap, planted and recovered

The deterministic hype-cycle generator plants a *known* gap and the IRR machinery recovers
it (a machinery proof, never market evidence):

| Synthetic tape | time-weighted CAGR | dollar-weighted IRR | gap (TWR − DWR) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Null — steady grower, flat flows | +11.6% | +15.7% | **−4.1 pts** |
| **Boom-bust + performance-chasing flows** | **+1.9%** | **−4.8%** | **+6.6 pts** |

On the steady-growth null the average dollar earns *more* than buy-and-hold (later, larger
dollars catch more compounding) — there is no behaviour penalty. On the boom-bust tape with
chasing flows the average dollar earns **−4.8%/yr while buy-and-hold earned +1.9%/yr** — a
**+6.6-point** behaviour gap, the buy-the-top penalty in miniature. The momentum overlay's
positive control is equally clean: on a no-momentum null its HAC *t* is −0.15; with planted
persistence it is **+5.24**.

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED.** The 50/200 trend overlay is the *only* signal to clear the bar on the
  real tape (HAC *t* = +2.09, bootstrap CI lower bound +0.22 bps) and it does so purely by
  going to cash through the 2021-22 crash; time-series momentum (*t* = +1.36) and
  mean-reversion (*t* = +0.33) are indistinguishable from noise. Real on the slow trend ·
  None on momentum/reversion.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The trend overlay's excess Sharpe over ARKK buy-and-hold is
  +0.07 and it underperforms a plain QQQ holding (Sharpe 0.93); the only "edge" is dodging
  a drawdown a QQQ investor never took. Nothing here is investable.
- **A buy-the-top machine? — CONFIRMED.** ARKK posted +13.8%/yr from inception but +737% of
  that arrived *before* the 2021 peak and the fund then fell −81%; the bulk of assets
  entered near the top, so the dollar-weighted return the average investor earned was deeply
  negative (Morningstar: ~$7–10bn of investor wealth destroyed). Chasing Cathie Wood was a
  buy-the-top machine, not a momentum win.
